source_book.author: Francis X. Weiser, S.J.
source_book.title: Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs

records.source_label: St Stephen's Day Wren Boys seasonal visiting and singing
records.source_report: Weiser describes decorated wren-bearing branches, door-to-door song, and receiving small gifts in the British Isles
records.geography: British Isles and particularly Ireland; specific Irish independent witnesses

secondary_witnesses.title: National Folklore Collection, Schools' Collection, Co. Kilkenny
Ireland National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage — Lá an Dreoilín

records.qualification: Historically documented seasonal folk tradition on St Stephen's Day; bird-killing details are historical description only and not recommended. An association with a saint's day does not establish liturgical status.

records.source_label: Horseshoe-shaped festive breads for St Stephen's Day
records.source_report: Weiser records women baking horseshoe-shaped special breads identified as podkovy for December 26
records.qualification: Single-author source observation only; shape, naming and region require original-language/independent corroboration.

records.source_label: Throwing walnuts during St Stephen's Day celebrations
records.source_report: Weiser states Polish children threw walnuts at each other on the feast
records.qualification: Reported folk game with author's own speculative historical interpretation kept separate from the action.

records.source_label: Blessed oats thrown toward priest and household animals on St Stephen's Day
records.source_report: Weiser describes blessed oats used playfully or ceremonially after Mass and around farm animals
records.geography: Poland and other unnamed regions as reported
records.qualification: Potential variant of existing hay/oats blessing, NOT automatically a new distinct custom.

records.source_label: Blessed salt and water kept for sick horses on St Stephen's Day
records.source_report: Weiser reports blessing salt and water for horses and reserving them for animal illness
records.qualification: Report of historical animal-related sacramental use; neither efficacy nor modern blessing rite confirmed.

records.source_report: Weiser records house-to-house visits in disguise during Christmas week, with altered dress and darkened faces
records.geography: England as described; exact geographic extent not checked
records.qualification: Historical secular and Christian-season folk overlap; not necessarily distinctively Catholic or a recommended religious practice.
